name: Luke Skywalker
summary: Luke leaves Tatooine to fight the Empire, learns from Obi-Wan and Yoda, and discovers that Vader is his father. His refusal to abandon that relationship helps bring about Vader’s final act of redemption. Later failures make him a fallible mentor rather than an unquestionable oracle.

name: Leia Organa

name: Han Solo
summary: Han begins as a self-interested smuggler concerned with payment and survival. His friendship with Chewbacca and growing attachment to Leia and Luke pull him into the rebellion. He repeatedly takes dangerous chances, and eventually confronts his son despite knowing that the encounter could kill him.

name: Yoda
summary: Yoda is an experienced teacher whose judgement is tested by the Jedi Order’s failure to recognise Palpatine’s plan. In exile he trains Luke through demanding lessons about fear and patience. Experience helps him interpret danger, but it does not prevent institutional mistakes.
source: Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Episode V)
Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (Episode VI)
Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)
Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)

name: Qui-Gon Jinn

source: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)

castingProfile.caution: Belief in a prophecy is interpretation, not proof of every future event.

name: Padmé Amidala

Her secret marriage and desire for peace create tensions between public responsibilities and personal trust.
source: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)
Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)
Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (Episode III)

source: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)
Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)

name: Finn

Returning for friends turns defection into an active choice to oppose his former organisation.
source: Star Wars: The Force Awakens (Episode VII)
Star Wars: The Last Jedi (Episode VIII)
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (Episode IX)

name: Darth Vader
summary: Anakin Skywalker, once a gifted pilot and Jedi, becomes the Emperor’s feared enforcer after his fall. Vader conceals the history behind his armour, hunts opposition and coerces subordinates. His final choice to save Luke shows that a chosen life stage matters: young podracer, fallen enforcer and redeemed father are one person.

name: Emperor Palpatine
summary: Palpatine presents himself as a legitimate politician while secretly directing a Sith plan. He exploits conflict, recruits an apprentice through fear of loss and converts emergency authority into Imperial rule. His threat comes from hidden responsibility and the ability to make others serve a project they misunderstand.

name: Maul
summary: In The Phantom Menace, Maul is the concealed Sith apprentice sent to attack the Jedi and support his master’s plan. His appearance exposes a threat thought absent for generations. This profile emphasises the film’s hunter and violent agent, rather than merging in later television-era criminal leadership.
source: Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)
Solo: A Star Wars Story

name: Count Dooku
summary: Dooku’s public identity as a former Jedi and Separatist leader hides his allegiance as Darth Tyranus. He organises opposition while serving the same Sith master who manipulates the Republic. His apparent independence therefore conceals a shared controller and a larger deception.
source: Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)
Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (Episode III)

name: General Grievous
summary: Grievous commands Separatist droid forces and collects the lightsabers of defeated Jedi. His intimidating presentation combines military authority with repeated attacks and the ability to disengage from danger. He provides a direct destructive contrast to villains whose power depends on political deceit.
source: Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (Episode III)

name: Grand Moff Tarkin
summary: Tarkin uses the Death Star as an instrument of public intimidation. The destruction of Alderaan demonstrates that his threats carry catastrophic consequences, but his confidence in Imperial superiority prevents him from accepting the station’s vulnerability. Authority and hubris operate together.
source: Star Wars: A New Hope (Episode IV)
Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (Episode III)
Rogue One: A Star Wars Story

His palace and the Boonta Eve race connect criminal power with public entertainment, making him a strong bridge between the films and a racing celebration.
source: Star Wars: A New Hope (Episode IV)
Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (Episode VI)
Star Wars: The Phantom Menace (Episode I)

source: Star Wars: A New Hope (Episode IV)
Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (Episode V)
Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (Episode VI)
Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)

His later return to Ben’s commitments makes identity, temptation and costly redemption distinct casting choices.
source: Star Wars: The Force Awakens (Episode VII)
Star Wars: The Last Jedi (Episode VIII)
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (Episode IX)

Star Wars: The Last Jedi (Episode VIII)

name: General Hux
summary: Hux directs First Order military operations while competing with Kylo for status. His resentment eventually leads him to leak information to the Resistance because he wants Kylo to lose. The leak is real but its motive is vindictive rivalry, not a conversion to the Resistance’s ideals.
source: Star Wars: The Force Awakens (Episode VII)
Star Wars: The Last Jedi (Episode VIII)
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (Episode IX)

source: Star Wars: The Force Awakens (Episode VII)
Star Wars: The Last Jedi (Episode VIII)

Star Wars: Attack of the Clones (Episode II)
Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (Episode III)

Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (Episode VI)

Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker (Episode IX)
